messages:
alex: seeing a sudden spike of 503s hitting the hosted gateway, started ~1713456700 and peaked around now. multiple customers reporting timeouts then 503s. can someone check upstream inference workers?

sre-bot: alert: upstream-infer-pool-12 pod/upstream-worker-12 terminated unexpectedly (signal 11)

amy-cs: FYI AcmeHealth reported 37% error rate on /v1/generate at 2024-11-15T10:42Z, customer id acme-392. CS escalated, they say requests are failing mid-stream then 503.

maria: grabbing logs now. initial glance: repeated lines of "cudaMalloc failed: out of memory" then a segfault. also seeing container restart loop on that node.

jon: paste from pod logs:
```
2024-11-15T10:40:12Z infer: allocating KV cache 1.2G
2024-11-15T10:40:12Z infer:error: cudaMalloc returned out of memory
2024-11-15T10:40:12Z infer:panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
2024-11-15T10:40:12Z kernel: [12345.6789] SIGSEGV at 0x0 in inference_runner
```

alex: thanks. looks like an OOM followed by a segfault (SIGSEGV) — probably in the runtime's prefetch / kv cache code. can we confirm GPU memory usage around the crash?

maria: ran `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` on node-43 for the window: GPU mem jumped from 43% to 98% over ~200ms before process exit. I also see burst in batch size in traces: some requests had batch_size=64 from the gateway while typical is 16.

jon: reproduction plan: run a short load test that mimics gateway batching pattern:
```
loadgen --target-host upstream-host-43 --model rdx-gpt-13b --concurrency 8 --seq-len 2048 --batching-pattern burst:64,16,16,16 --duration 5m
```

amy-cs: customer requests: they send long prompts (2k tokens) and enable streaming; might be triggering large KV allocations. they also said their traffic had a short spike.

alex: immediate mitigations: 1) throttle gateway batching for hosted tier A to max_batch=32 2) put fallback routing to a lower-memory model variant for heavy-context requests 3) cordon node-43 and drain to stop noisy restarts while we debug.

maria: applied temporary gateway config: set max_batch_size=32 for route /v1/generate (rolled for 2 minutes) — monitoring now. also filed a k8s drain: `kubectl cordon node-43 && kubectl drain node-43 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`

jon: created a capture on the crashed container: `gcore` + core path uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/cores/upstream-12-1713456789.core` — stack shows crash in `kv_prefetch.cpp:142` during `reserve_kv` path. attaching stack snippet:
```
#0 0x7f8a1234 in reserve_kv at kv_prefetch.cpp:142
#1 0x7f8a1300 in prefetch_sequence at prefetcher.cpp:88
#2 0x7f8a1400 in runner_loop at runner.cpp:415
```

alex: good capture. assign ownership: jon will lead for core analysis + repro, maria will own short-term mitigation (gateway throttle + node cordon), amy-cs to keep customer updated.

amy-cs: I told AcmeHealth that we're throttling bursts and investigating; asked for a sample request that failed. they sent a sanitized prompt and a timestamp — uploaded to the incident folder.

maria: observation: the problem correlates with a recent runtime change that swapped in a new kv allocation path (deployed 2024-11-14 03:12 UTC). rollback candidate is `runtime:v3.4.1` -> previous stable `v3.3.8`.

alex: ops decision: roll runtime back on the affected pool to v3.3.8 while we confirm fix. coordinate with releases to avoid mass impact.

jon: quick repro done on a dev node using loadgen above + the customer prompt — reproduced segfault within 90s. will instrument with ASAN build to get more details.

maria: rollback started on pool-12 (drain, patch deployment image -> v3.3.8, rollout). monitoring metrics: error-rate for route dropped from 22% -> 3% on that pool after instances came up.

amy-cs: customer note: AcmeHealth confirms failures subsided after ~6 minutes, but wants postmortem and billing credit for the window.

alex: next steps: jon to open GH issue with crash reproducible steps + stack + core, label P1-runtime, patch kv reserve path; maria to write rollback timeline and config changes; amy-cs to draft customer-facing summary and credit proposal; schedule incident postmortem tomorrow 11/16 9am PT.

jon: preliminary root cause hypothesis: kv prefetch reserve path didn't properly handle rapid allocation failures under bursty batching, left a null pointer leading to SIGSEGV. fix will add allocation guards + backoff + unit test for burst sequences.

amy-cs: marking this thread for follow-up with customer; will attach transcripts and timeline to the support ticket.

alex: thanks team. once we have the GH issue and a short changelist for the fix I'll update the incident channel and close the triage. :thumbsup:
